title: docs(spec): the runAs description names a system run's refused identity-assignment writes, with its ADR-0087 D3 entry
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6JaoVgqGdGWoJtcHYXUFi5Es7m)_

Closes #25554
Part of #25251

Clause-②: no (describe text and ADR registration only; no accept-set change)
Metadata-protocol: semantic (records the change of meaning #25483 landed)

This is PR2 of ruling 6354966423 (letter B) on #25251, the spec-lane half. PR1, #25483, made the data middleware refuse a `runAs: 'system'` flow's governed writes to the four identity-assignment objects. The published `FlowSchema.runAs` description still told authors that a system flow keeps system privileges without exception. Under ADR-0087 this PR has to ship in the same release as #25483.

## What changed

- **`packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`, the `runAs` describe.** One new sentence: elevation does not reach identity assignment. A system run's governed writes (insert, update, delete, transfer, restore, purge) to `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_invitation` and `sys_member` are refused with `PERMISSION_DENIED`. Declare `user` for position holdings and permission-set grants, so the ADR-0090 D12 delegated-administration gate judges the user the run acts for. Change invitations and memberships through the organization endpoints.
- **The comment block above `runAs`.** The same rule stated exactly as #25483 enforces it: refused ahead of the `isSystem` bypass for a context carrying `isSystem` AND a `flowRunId`, `403`, nothing written. Reads of the four objects and writes to every other object are unchanged, and so is a platform writer whose system context carries no flow run.
- **ADR-0087 D3 semantic entry** `flow-run-as-system-identity-assignment-write-refused` (`entries/semantic/18.…`), the entry #25483's changeset left to this PR. It has no D2 conversion: changing `runAs` changes what every other node of the flow may do, and an endpoint call is not a rewrite of a node.
- **Derived pages regenerated** with `gen:docs` (`content/docs/references/automation/flow.mdx`, `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx`). `gen:skill-refs` and `gen:skill-docs` produced no change. `registry.ts`, `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide are generated and git-ignored, so nothing is committed for them.
- **Changeset** `25554-runas-identity-assignment-wording.md`, `@objectstack/spec` `minor`, with the registered ADR-0087 disposition marker.

## Acceptance notes

- **ADR-0073 amendment not in this PR.** `check-governed-merges --test` answers GOVERNED (Tier H) for `docs/adr/0073-automation-execution-identity.md`, so per the card it goes as a separate maintainer-merged PR. The draft text is in the os-dev-report on #25554.
- **Changeset level is `minor`, not `patch`.** Ruling A (2026-10-21, on #25105), as `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces it, requires at least one moved package at `minor` for `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. The dispatch order said `patch`; the gate wins.
- `service-automation/src/engine.ts` still quotes the earlier ruling text ("system flows keep system privileges") as a citation of that ruling. It is left alone.

## Verification

At head `5a9bf414cf`:

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 109 families for this diff. 108 exit 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3: it needs every workspace package built), and CI measures it.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` green. `vitest run src/migrations src/automation/flow` in `@objectstack/spec` passed 25 files and 1122 tests.
- `check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide`, `check:docs`, `check:skill-refs`, `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` and `check-changeset-no-major --base origin/main` are green.
